sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Financial Market News Aggregation and Syndication Feed

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (Fifth Republic; unitary state; no separate sub-state incorporation registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic codification: French Commercial Code, Civil Code, Monetary and Financial Code; precedents of the Cour de cassation and CJEU apply)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–US Income Tax Treaty (1994, as amended by 2006 Protocol)
France–Germany Income Tax Treaty (1959, as amended by 1989/2015 protocols)
France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (1984, as adjusted by the EU Lisbon transfer of BIT competence)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Arts. L.561-1 to L.561-57 (AML/CFT and beneficial-owner declaration), as amended by Order No. 2020-115 and Decree No. 2021-325; CMF Arts. L.561-45 to L.561-49 (bénéficiaires effectifs filed with the RCS via the Guichet unique); Commercial Code Arts. L.223-1 et seq. (SARL); FATF Recommendations transposed; EU Regulation 2015/847 (wire-transfer information) for Swift/USD rails.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_identification_notes: Disclosure is mandatory even below the 25% threshold when the person exercises, alone or jointly, direct or indirect control over the company (CMF Art. L.561-2-2 and R.561-1/2); public access is restricted after CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 — the RCS portal does not publish the UBO file.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate extract (certificat de bonne tenue / good standing certificate) of each non-French corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if origin state is not a Hague Convention party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each individual UBO (foreign-issued)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry / police authority of the UBO's country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) of each UBO, not older than 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank in the UBO's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy + Apostille (where obtainable); otherwise certified sworn declaration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) appointing the French incorporation agent/manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of criminal record / Certificate of non-conviction of the proposed manager (gérant), if available in origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records authority of the manager's country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed UBOs, managers, and financing counterparties against: (i) French RST/Gels list (Fichier national des gels) and TRACFIN instructions; (ii) EU consolidated financial sanctions under Council Regulation (EU) 269/2014 and relevant CFSP decisions; (iii) UN Security Council consolidated lists (ISIL/Al-Qaida 1267/1988 and DPRK 1718); (iv) domestic police databases (FPR/FIJ) for criminal-adverse indicators; (v) OFAC SDN and 50% Rule screening as a contractual prerequisite of Swift USD wire and US-dollar clearing; and (vi) FATF Recommendation 12 PEP checks including family members and close associates (CMF Arts. L.561-10 and R.561-5). The company itself, as a news-aggregation activity under ISIC 6391, does not meet the CMF Art. L.561-2 obligated-entity criteria and holds a 'Low_Risk_Standard' risk tier; however, all EU/UN sanctions and PEP checks remain mandatory for transaction counterparties and beneficial owners.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique de l'INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) — official portal for RCS/RNCS formalities; name verification via 'data.inpi.fr' (RNCS search) and EUIPO eSearch (trademarks); Infogreffe is a non-authoritative mirror.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The dénomination sociale must be written in Latin/Roman script and may be composed of words of any language as long as they are readable in French legal documents; foreign-script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for the RCS. The name must be lawful, not contrary to ordre public, and not misleading as to the SARL's object. A distinct generic element and an indication of legal form ('SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée') are mandatory (Code de commerce Arts. R.123-53, L.223-1; décret d'application).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Banking (requires ACPR credit-institution authorization)
Assurance, Assureur, Insurance (requires ACPR insurance authorization)
Société de gestion, Asset Management, Gestion sous mandat (requires AMF authorization)
Bourse, Stock Exchange, Euronext, CAC 40 (registered/exclusive marks of operators)
Bloomberg, Reuters, Dow Jones, FactSet, Nasdaq, S&P 500 (third-party trademarks requiring consent)
Avocat, Expert-Comptable, Notaire, Huissier, Commissaire aux comptes (regulated professions)
Ministère, Administration, Police, Gendarmerie, République, État (state-authority implication)
Crédit, Prêt, Financement, Épargne (misleading financial-service implications for a newswire product)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_reservation_note: French law does not operate a common-law style pre-incorporation name reservation; the name is conditionally cleared at the time of filing the incorporation dossier with the RCS/Guichet unique and becomes definitively protected on RCS entry. The 30-day period reflects the administrative validity of the pre-filing negative-search report (INPI anticipation report and trademark clearance opinion) used to coordinate the filing and to ensure no intervening identical registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the guichet (INPI) rejects the dénomination sociale or the RCS clerk refuses registration, the applicant receives a reasoned notification. The applicant may (i) refile a corrected name without additional fees; (ii) submit an administrative request ('recours gracieux') to the RCS clerk/INPI within 2 months under Code de justice administrative; (iii) seek judicial rectification before the Président du tribunal de commerce (Médiation/CNC) in the same 2-month window; or (iv) appeal any trademark-based refusal to the Cour d'appel de Paris within 1 month (CPI Art. R.411-19 for INPI trademark decisions). Parallel filing under a secondary name is expressly disrecommended as it triggers double publication costs.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.optional_trademark_filing: Where the newswire brand has multiple markets, a parallel EUIPO trademark application (Class 38 news transmission; Class 41 financial-information publications; Class 9 API software) should be filed simultaneously; official fees €850 for one class, €900 for two classes (electronic filing, EUIPO fee schedule 2024).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_basis: SARL must maintain a siège social in France (Code de commerce Art. L.223-1; Art. R.123-91); address must appear on all corporate documents; commerçant registration requires the RCS domicile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible: a licensed domiciliation company ('centre d'affaires' under Code de commerce Arts. L.123-11-2 and L.123-11-3) may act as the registered office, provided a written domiciliation agreement is in place, the address is a physical French location, and the manager can attend the registered office; the manager's own dwelling may be used for up to 5 years (Art. L.123-11-1). A pure virtual mailbox at a non-physical address is impermissible for an RCS-registered SARL.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 10% cumulative probability of an unannounced or documented inspection within the first three tax years. DGFiP tax audits always follow formal notice; RCS clerical controls are documentary; labour inspections (DREETS) are unlikely with zero employees; ministerial KYC inspections do not apply because the company is not an AML-obligated entity. Documentary substance (contracts, invoices, domain/API infrastructure, server records) should be preserved to defeat any anti-abuse domicile reclassification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.223-1 through L.223-43; L.123-1 and L.123-3 (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet unique de formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts of the SARL (Articles of Association) together with the standard RCS incorporation declaration (CERFA Form N° 11676).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum; founders may set share capital from €1. Cash contributions must be deposited in a specially opened blocked account with a French credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary, and are released only upon registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT each subscriber listed in the subscription schedule accepts the shares allocated to him or her, fully paid as provided in the statuts. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the company's registered office is established at the address placed at the disposal of the company by the gérant. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the subscriber associates together appoint [Name] as Gérant of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée for an unrestricted term, with full powers to act on behalf of the company, to open any bank or payment accounts, and to represent the company in all ordinary administrative and contractual matters. RESOLVED FINALLY THAT the Gérant is authorised and instructed to complete and file the statutory incorporation dossier via the Guichet unique, pay all applicable fees, and procure final registration on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of statutory bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting collectively; optional notaire in case of in-kind contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in compliance with mandatory SARL provisions, defining the share capital, share subscription schedule, registered office address, corporate object conforming to ISIC 6391 financial news aggregation, and the powers of the gérant. Execute the statuts either by private signature or before a notaire when a contribution in-kind requires a statutory auditor's valuation report.
required_dossiers: Fully executed statuts signed by all shareholders
Passport or national ID copies of all shareholders and the gérant
Certificate of beneficial ownership when required
Proof of availability of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any incompleteness in the draft, obtain a notarial correction or appointment of a commissaire aux apports where in-kind contributions are used, and re-execute the statuts with unanimous shareholder consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of paid-up capital and issuance of blocked account certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or notaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company being formed, deposit all cash contributions into such blocked account, and obtain a bank certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds) itemising the amount and each subscriber. In-kind contributions must be fully described in the statuts and, where subject to a statutory valuation, covered by the commissaire aux apports report lodged at the registry.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of deposit of cash contributions
Statutory auditor's report on in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank refuses deposit or certification, cure by obtaining a certificate from a notaire or by regularising the subscription schedule and filing an amended deposit documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of legal announcement and submission to the single business portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcement journal authorised in the department; INPI Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a mandatory legal announcement (avis de constitution) in a journal d'annonces légales of the department of the registered office. Thereafter submit the complete electronic incorporation dossier on the Guichet unique, attaching the statuts, announcement proof, bank certificate and declarations. Provide all shareholder and manager declarations, including non-conviction attestation for the gérant.
required_dossiers: Proof of publication of the legal announcement
CERFA N° 11676 incorporating full company data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal rejects for missing or inconsistent data, supplement the application within the statutory delay using the online rectification workflow, pay any additional fee, and resubmit for a fresh review by the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration on the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés and Kbis issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Guichet unique transmits the validated dossier, the Greffe conducts legal review and records the SARL on the national RCS. Upon registration, the company obtains its SIREN/SIRET number and the RCS extract (Kbis extract), which serves as the statutory proof of incorporation and good standing.
required_dossiers: Completed and accepted digital dossier from Guichet unique
Receipt of payment of registry fees
Copies of the published legal announcement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a query or refusal based on mandatory information, cure by complying with the written observations, filing amended statuts if required, and requesting re-examination within the applicable legal window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités (DREETS) – no industrial operating licence required for a non-manufacturing digital financial newswire service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – company is a non-industrial digital information service under ISIC 6391, not an ICPE installation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique – Direction générale de la prévention des risques
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No fixed industrial installation, no emissions discharge; only tertiary office presence with de minimis environmental footprint
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial effluent; residual obligations limited to general waste management, office equipment e-waste recycling under DEEE regulations, and adherence to digital infrastructure eco-design best practices.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-risk assessment and safety certification for tertiary ERP premises (e.g., Aménagement du Code du travail on means of escape), workplace electrical installation certification, compliance with workplace health and safety codes, and declaration of the premises to the competent municipal fire authority if visitor capacity exceeds applicable ERP threshold.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE) for non-established businesses; principal portals: impots.gouv.fr and the formalities portal operated through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the French SARL through the Guichet unique; the filing is transmitted to the Registre national des entreprises and results in attribution of a SIREN and SIRET. 2. Open and maintain the corporate tax account with the competent Service des impôts des entreprises. 3. Apply to the competent DGFiP office for VAT registration where the company conducts taxable French transactions, makes intra-Community transactions, imports goods, or cannot rely on a reverse-charge mechanism. 4. For a non-established foreign entity, submit the VAT registration application and supporting documents to the SIEE, generally including constitutional documents, commercial activity evidence, identification of directors and beneficial owners, tax residence evidence, power of attorney where applicable, and French or translated banking and invoicing information. 5. DGFiP issues a French VAT number in the format FR plus a two-digit key and the entity's nine-digit SIREN. The SIREN is the principal French business identifier; France does not generally issue a separate income-tax TIN equivalent to the SIREN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Certain SARLs may elect income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu), including a qualifying family SARL without the ordinary five-year limitation, or an eligible closely held SARL for a maximum period generally limited to five fiscal years, subject to statutory ownership, size, activity, non-listing, and shareholder conditions. There is no United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework and do not provide a general elective hybrid classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), administered under the French Code général des impôts and EU VAT rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For French-established businesses eligible for the franchise en base de TVA, the principal turnover thresholds are generally EUR 37,500 for services and EUR 85,000 for sales of goods, with tolerance thresholds generally of EUR 41,250 and EUR 93,500 respectively. These thresholds determine eligibility for the small-business exemption and are subject to statutory adjustments and sector-specific rules. A non-established taxable person generally cannot rely on the French domestic threshold in the same manner and may require registration from the first taxable French transaction. Registration may also be required independently of turnover for imports, intra-Community acquisitions, distance sales, or transactions not subject to an applicable reverse charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting through accredited private platforms (plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, or PDPs), with data transmission to the public invoicing portal. The reformed timetable provides mandatory receipt of electronic invoices for all French-established businesses from 1 September 2026; mandatory issuance applies from 1 September 2026 to large enterprises and tax groups, from 1 September 2027 to medium-sized enterprises, SMEs, and micro-enterprises, subject to statutory transition rules. B2B domestic invoices must use prescribed structured or hybrid formats and include required invoice data. E-reporting applies to specified cross-border and B2C transactions. France does not operate a universal pre-clearance requirement for every invoice comparable to jurisdictions requiring real-time invoice approval; PDP transmission, data validation, archiving, and reporting obligations apply according to the applicable timetable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT under the French implementation of the EU export exemption where the supplier or an authorized intermediary establishes that the goods left the EU customs territory and the transaction, supplier, and customs records correspond. Evidence normally includes the export customs declaration and electronic exit confirmation, commonly demonstrated through the Movement Reference Number and Export Control System records, together with commercial and transport documentation. Services supplied to a business established outside France are generally governed by place-of-supply rules rather than a French 0% export rate; qualifying B2B services are generally outside the scope of French VAT with customer-side reverse charge in the country of establishment. Specific rules apply to services directly connected with exported goods, intermediated transactions, transport, digital services, and B2C supplies. Input VAT refunds require valid invoices, business-purpose evidence, and compliance with the applicable domestic or non-established-business refund procedure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration, including the export MRN and evidence of acceptance and exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or equivalent
Proof of physical exit or delivery outside the EU, including ECS exit results, carrier confirmation, or equivalent customs evidence
Purchase orders, contracts, and shipping records linking the exported goods to the invoiced transaction
Payment evidence or receivables records where relevant to substantiate the transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not a general French statutory export-VAT document
Import or destination-country customs evidence where necessary to resolve discrepancies or support an audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation requirement for export VAT relief. The decisive requirements are valid export evidence, actual exit from the EU customs territory, correct invoicing, and consistency between customs, accounting, transport, and payment records. If the exemption or refund is unsupported, DGFiP may assess the unpaid VAT retrospectively, together with late-payment interest and applicable penalties. Deliberate non-compliance may attract a 40% penalty; fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct may attract an 80% penalty, subject to statutory facts and procedural safeguards. False documentation, fictitious exports, or organized VAT fraud may also create criminal exposure. The statute of limitations generally permits VAT reassessment for the relevant statutory period, commonly three years, subject to extension or special rules for fraud and criminal proceedings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) as the prudential supervisory authority; the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) oversees balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member with full capital and current account convertibility under EU Treaty provisions (Articles 63-66 TFEU). Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to standard corporate tax withholding (if applicable) and anti-money laundering (AML) verification. No exchange control approval is required for cross-border transfers, but all transactions exceeding €10,000 must be reported to the French customs and tax authorities for statistical and AML purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds exists in France. Exporters may retain foreign currency in designated accounts, but must report all cross-border flows to the Banque de France via the balance-of-payments reporting system (REP) within 20 business days of the transaction. No minimum conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte Courant) and Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) for share capital deposits
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (for corporate treasury) and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. France recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under PSD2, and cross-border EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Qonto, or N26) can open accounts remotely. However, for a financial newswire with syndicated finance data, the bank's AML risk assessment may classify the business as 'financial services' requiring enhanced due diligence. EMIs are viable for operational liquidity but not for capital escrow or complex trade finance. Legal constraints: EMIs cannot provide credit or hold client funds beyond e-money limits; they are not suitable for large syndicated finance settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For SARL entities, French banks generally require at least one director or authorized signatory to appear in person for the initial KYC interview, especially for capital escrow accounts. Remote opening is permitted for operational accounts if the bank uses video identification (e.g., via ACPR-approved e-IDV solutions), but the final approval often requires a physical visit or a notarized power of attorney. For non-resident directors, a physical visit to the bank branch or a French consulate may be mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business sector flagged as 'financial information services' (ISIC 6391) – potential for market abuse or insider trading concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Detailed business plan and revenue model (API subscription, syndicated news feed); (2) Client contracts with licensed financial institutions; (3) Compliance manual demonstrating adherence to EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) and GDPR; (4) Proof of data licensing agreements; (5) Beneficial ownership declaration (French RBE registry extract); (6) Source of funds for initial capital injection (bank statements, notarized gift/deed).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or directors – increased PEP or sanctions screening risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Passport copies and proof of address for all directors/shareholders; (2) CVs and professional references; (3) Sanctions and PEP screening results from a recognized provider (e.g., World-Check); (4) Tax residency certificates; (5) Explanation of the corporate structure and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of cross-border wire transfers (inbound/outbound) – potential for money laundering or terrorist financing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Cash flow forecast and transaction volume estimates; (2) Client due diligence files for all counterparties; (3) Internal AML/CFT procedures and training records; (4) Designation of a compliance officer (Déclarant Tracfin); (5) Audit trail of all transactions via a recognized treasury management system.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'S010' (Capital contribution) or 'S020' (Shareholder loan). For EU transfers, use SEPA CT with purpose code 'COST' or 'CAPC'. Verification: The bank will require the capital escrow account to be opened before injection; the transfer must reference the SARL's SIREN number and the notarized articles of association. For non-EU transfers, include the LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) and a copy of the board resolution authorizing the capital increase.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to suppliers or licensors; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) via SWIFT MT700 for high-value syndicated finance data licensing; (3) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for EU-based operational payments; (4) For API-based subscription revenue, use Stripe Connect or similar payment gateways with automatic settlement to the operational account. All outbound transfers must include the correct purpose code (e.g., 'S030' for royalties, 'S040' for service fees) and be reported to the Banque de France if exceeding €10,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain vanilla) – permitted for hedging currency exposure on non-EUR receivables/payables, subject to ACPR authorization if the SARL is not a financial entity.
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – permissible for exotic currencies (e.g., CNY, INR) where deliverable forwards are restricted; must be executed via a licensed bank.
Currency Swaps – allowed for long-term hedging of syndicated finance cash flows, but require board approval and documented risk management policy.
FX Options – permitted for hedging but not for speculative purposes; must be aligned with the underlying commercial exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (Bilan, Comptes de Résultat and Annexe) with Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to €1,500; risk of dissolution proceedings if not rectified

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation with updates required within 30 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €10,000; potential criminal sanctions for willful non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000 or total assets exceed €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review and update of beneficial owners information in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs; any changes must be declared within 30 days

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Impôt sur les Sociétés, standard rate for fiscal years beginning on or after 01/01/2022); 15% reduced rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with EUR <10M turnover and >75% individual/qualifying corporate shareholding; effective top marginal rate 25.83% for companies paying the 3.3% social contribution on the tax due.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate on first EUR 42,500 of profit (SME); Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million (annual cap); Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenses for SMEs up to EUR 400k; parent-subsidiary regime (95% dividend deduction) and French Pillar Two DMTT (15% minimum tax) for groups with consolidated revenue >= EUR 750 million.
